linkedin.hook: We migrated Goldie — the catering concierge agent for Golden Plate Events — from Retell to ElevenLabs in 4 working days. Here's the diff.
linkedin.body:
Goldie is a 24/7 inbound voice agent across all five NYC boroughs. Answers calls, qualifies leads, captures event context, posts to the CRM. Live for months.

Why we migrated:
· Voice quality — ElevenLabs is in a different class for prosody and the "this sounds like a person" threshold
· Tooling depth — structured tool calling, dynamic context injection, native conversation evaluator we can wire into our own eval pipeline

Day 1 — Pulled the prompt + 60 representative transcripts from the last 90 days. Transcripts mattered more than the prompt; they show what the agent actually does, which is always different from what the prompt says it should do.

Day 2 — Ported prompt + 4 tools (qualify_lead, capture_event_context, schedule_callback, post_to_crm). CRM endpoint stayed identical.

Day 3 — Parallel deploy on a separate Twilio number. 10% of calls to the new agent for two days. Both versions tagged in the CRM for side-by-side lead quality comparison.

Day 4 — Lead quality equal-or-better across all four scoring dimensions. Customer-side voice naturalness materially higher. Cutover. Eval suite live the same day.

What got better: 3 customers in week 1 mentioned unprompted they didn't realize they were talking to AI.

What broke: first-turn latency was ~400ms slower (fixed with pre-warmed greeting). Tool returning timezone-aware dates broke our CRM ingest (one-line fix, but parallel deploy caught it).

What we'd do differently: parallel deploy on day 1, not day 3. And write the eval suite before porting the prompt — old evals tested for behaviors the old agent had, not behaviors the new one needed.

Goldie answers inbound catering calls 24/7 across all 5 NYC boroughs. Qualifies leads, captures event context, posts to CRM. Been live for months.

Why migrate:
· Voice quality — ElevenLabs is in a different class
· Tooling — structured calls, dynamic context, native evals

We didn't replace it. We replaced the substrate.
Day 1: Pulled prompt + 60 transcripts. Transcripts > prompt. Always.
Day 2: Ported prompt + 4 tools. CRM endpoint identical. The only thing changing was the agent calling it.

Day 3: Parallel deploy on a separate Twilio number. 10% of calls to new agent. Both versions tagged in CRM for side-by-side lead-quality compare.

This is non-negotiable for voice migrations.
Day 4: Lead quality equal-or-better. Naturalness materially higher. Cutover. Evals live same day.

Wins: 3 customers in week 1 said unprompted they didn't know it was AI.
Gotchas: 400ms first-turn latency (pre-warmed greeting), timezone-aware dates broke ingest (parallel deploy caught it).

Next time: parallel deploy day 1, not day 3. And write evals BEFORE porting — old suite tested for old-agent behaviors.
